findings.inference: The per-program scalar cost is flat (0.505-0.687 us, i.e. +/-15%) while the work per program spans 128 to 4096 elements (32x) and BLOCK spans 128 to 4096. There is therefore no measurable per-element component: kernel time is ~ Block Num * 0.62 us / 20 AI cores. This single law reproduces every measurement: timing-5 32768*0.62/20 = 1016 us vs 1219 us observed, timing-4 254 vs 308, timing-3 63 vs 80, timing-2 508 vs 610. It explains why the deficit grows exactly with program count (0.13x at 32768 programs, 0.51x at 16384, 1.0-1.5x at 1024-2048) and why the achieved store throughput is only 27.5 GB/s at timing-5 against 214 GB/s implied by the eval reference latency (33.55 MB / 0.15662 ms) and 440 GB/s actually achieved at timing-14. The 20-core normalization uses target.num_sm=20 from the eval context.

findings.inference: Doubling the stored bytes at fixed geometry changes the wall time by 0.1% while the store-pipeline share rises from 19.8% to 26.7%. The kernel is not store-bandwidth bound at these program counts; the fixed per-program component absorbs the difference. The same control also explains the parent's observation that fp16 8192^2 and fp32 8192^2 both cost ~0.61 ms: the eval speedups differ (0.52x vs 1.05x) only because the reference bandwidth is dtype-independent while the candidate is overhead-limited.

findings.label: Masked-store element-wise predication is NOT the bottleneck (hypothesis b contradicted)
findings.backend_detail: aiv_vec_time at timing-5 is 58.4 us of a 1219.5 us kernel; at timing-3 3.4 us of 79.9 us.
findings.inference: If the masked store (tl.store(..., mask=off<red) at main.py:59) were lowered to per-element predication, its scalar cost would scale with BLOCK and the vector pipe would carry the payload. Instead the vector-pipeline share stays at 4.3-9.9% for every block size and the per-program scalar cost is flat (and even slightly decreasing) as BLOCK grows 32x. The mask/predicate generation is therefore amortized/vectorized, not per-element. Reducing the mask cannot recover the 0.13x case; changing it is a secondary cleanup (all 18 timing workloads have BLOCK == red by construction of _pow2_at_most, so the mask is provably all-true there).

findings.label: The per-program constant is consistent with one exposed round trip to the two scalar loads of grad[o] and idx[o]
findings.backend_detail: Ascend scalar pipe reports the stall as scalar occupancy; MTE2 time counts DMA busy time only, so an idle-but-waiting load never appears in aiv_mte2_time.
findings.inference: Each program issues only two scalar loads (main.py:56-57) whose results are required before the value compare and store can be formed, and the load pipeline is essentially never busy (mte2 ratio 0.0019, 1.99 us total). A ~0.5-0.7 us per-program scalar-pipe occupancy for a handful of instructions is the shape of an exposed latency, not of throughput, and 0.5-0.7 us is the order of an HBM round trip on this part. Because the deficit scales linearly with program count and shows no overlap benefit at 32768 blocks, each program is paying that latency once and largely unamortized. I cannot separate this from block dispatch/teardown with the counters that ran; both are per-program constants and both are reduced by the same change, so confidence is medium for the mechanism and high for the scaling law.

performance_interpretation: The eval geo_mean of 0.685 is produced by one regime: the fast path launches one program per contiguous `red`-element row (grid=(1, outer)), so program count equals outer and every program independently re-pays a fixed ~0.5-0.7 us of scalar-pipe work. Measured across eight profiles, that fixed cost is independent of BLOCK (128..4096), of dtype (fp16 vs fp32 at identical geometry: 610 vs 609 us), and of elements per program (128..4096), while the vector pipe never exceeds 9.9% utilization. Consequences are geometric, not marginal: timing-5 (outer=32768, red=512) writes 33.55 MB at 27.5 GB/s versus 214 GB/s implied by the 0.157 ms reference; timing-4 (outer=8192, red=256) writes 4.19 MB at 13.6 GB/s. The regime is not masked-store predication (vector share is flat across block sizes) and not store bandwidth (2x bytes at fixed geometry costs nothing), and there is no evidence of a UB/double-buffer limit: tile sizes are only 0.25-8 KB, far below the 192 KB UB, and the kernel never reports icache misses or spills. Only the fp32 8192^2 case (timing-14) is genuinely near the achievable ceiling at 440 GB/s versus 419 GB/s for the reference, because its `outer` is small relative to its 268 MB payload. The frozen hypothesis was right that a single fused zero-fill+write launch is the correct architecture, and wrong in its expectation that the fused kernel would 'at least match reference bandwidth on the large memsets' at one row per program, which it misses by up to 8x. Small shapes are already at the practical floor (timing-3: 79.9 us kernel vs 103.2 us eval latency, i.e. ~23 us host overhead), so the recoverable loss is concentrated in the many-program shapes.

next_experiment.action_description: In _vsrb_lastdim_kernel make each program own ROWS consecutive `outer` rows instead of one. Build a 2D tile of shape [ROWS, BLOCK] with BLOCK = pow2 at most red (do not shrink BLOCK below red when red is a power of two), load grad/idx as length-ROWS vectors, compute val = tl.where(cols[None, :] == idx[:, None], g[:, None], 0.0), and store the resulting contiguous [ROWS*red] output region. Reduce grid to (nblk, ceil(outer/ROWS)). Sizes measured here: ROWS=8 for red=512 (timing-5/11/17: 32768 -> 4096 programs), ROWS=8 for red=256 (timing-4/10/16: 8192 -> 1024), ROWS=4 for red=1024 (timing-0/6/9/12/15: 1024 -> 256), ROWS=4 with BLOCK=8192 for red=8192 (timing-2/8/14: 16384 -> 2048). Keep ROWS as a constexpr defaulting to 1 so rollback is a one-line change, and keep the existing masked path whenever red is not a power of two or ROWS == 1. Leave num_warps at its default for this round so the result is attributable to the tile shape alone.
next_experiment.expected_impact: The measured law (time ~ Block Num * 0.62 us / 20 cores) predicts timing-5 kernel time to fall from 1219 us to ~127 us of fixed cost plus a ~80-157 us store floor, i.e. ~200 us and ~0.8x versus the 0.157 ms reference instead of 0.13x; timing-4 from 308 us to ~60 us; timing-0 from 33-39 us to ~10-15 us (bounded by the ~23 us host overhead visible as 79.9 us kernel vs 103.2 us eval on timing-3). timing-2/timing-8 should move from 0.52x toward ~0.75-0.9x and timing-14 should be roughly unchanged at ~1.05x because it is already near the 420-440 GB/s ceiling. Headline geo_mean expected to rise from 0.685 to roughly 0.95-1.10.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: UB pressure: the int32 offset tensor is ROWS*red*4 bytes (ROWS=8, red=512 -> 16 KB) plus the fp16 value tile; keep ROWS so that ROWS*red*4 <= 32 KB and fall back to a smaller ROWS rather than shrinking BLOCK below red, which would reintroduce masking. Correctness: consecutive rows must write disjoint output ranges (they do, out is contiguous with stride red), and each row must use its own idx/g; the general inner>1 kernel and any red that is not a power of two must keep the current path. The 2D store must remain contiguous per row to avoid a strided MTE3 regression; verify on timing-5 that aiv_mte3_ratio does not spike. Rollback: set ROWS=1 (constexpr default) to restore exactly the current kernel, then re-run preflight and eval.
success_criteria: All 78 correctness workloads still PASSED with abs_err=0 and rel_err=0.
Headline geo_mean strictly above the current 0.6851, with a target of >= 1.0.
timing-5, timing-11 and timing-17 reach >= 0.6x speedup (from 0.13x), i.e. eval latency <= 0.26 ms.
timing-4, timing-10 and timing-16 reach >= 0.85x (from ~0.51x) and timing-2/timing-8 reach >= 0.70x (from ~0.52x).
No workload regresses by more than 5% versus its current value: timing-14 stays >= 1.00x and the small-shape workloads stay >= 1.40x.

Profiler confirmation on the next round: msprof Block Num for timing-5 drops from 32768 to ~4096 and aiv_scalar_ratio falls below 0.50 (from 0.86), showing the per-program cost was amortized rather than hidden.

open_questions: Is the ~0.62 us per program block dispatch/teardown, or the exposed HBM round trip of the two scalar loads at main.py:56-57? The rows-per-program experiment is a joint test: if time falls ~8x at 8 fewer programs, the cost was amortizable per-program overhead; if it falls much less, part of the cost is intrinsic to block dispatch on this target.
Does the row-batched 2D tile stay within UB at ROWS=4 and red=8192 (fp32: 8192*4*4 B of int32 offsets = 128 KB, close to the 192 KB limit)? A ROWS=2 fallback may be needed for the fp32 8192^2 case.

Would an unmasked store (valid whenever BLOCK == red, true for all 18 timing workloads) buy anything measurable, given the mask is already vectorized? It is cheap to include but is not expected to move the headline metric.
